content.title: Celtics-Raptors recap: The Jays, Queta stay hot in C's win at TD Garden
content.text: What to KnowKayla Burton and Noa Dalzell shared more postgame reaction on the Celtics Talk Podcast.Jayson Tatum (23 points, 13 rebounds, seven assists) notched his ninth double-double in 14 games.Neemias Queta tallied 18 points, seven rebounds, four assists and three blocks.Jaylen Brown finished with a game-high 26 points (11-20 FG).Boston completed a 4-0 season sweep of Toronto. The Boston Celtics treated the TD Garden crowd to a 115-101 win over the Toronto Raptors on Easter Sunday. Boston scored a whopping 76 points in the paint, with Jaylen Brown (26 points) and Jayson Tatum (23 points) leading the way. Tatum recorded his ninth double-double in 14 games, as he added 13 rebounds and seven assists. Neemias Queta also has another big day for Boston. The big man tallied 18 points (16 in the first half) with seven rebounds, four assists, and three blocks. Check out our live blog below for a full recap of Sunday's game: The Boston Celtics completed a 4-0 season sweep of the Toronto Raptors as they won their Easter Sunday showdown at TD Garden, 115-101. Jayson Tatum again starred for the C's as he continues to look more like himself post-Achilles injury. After notching a triple-double in Wednesday's win over Miami and coming one assist shy of a triple-double in Friday's win in Milwaukee, Tatum finished with 23 points, 13 rebounds, and seven assists against Toronto. He has recorded nine double-doubles in his 14 games played this season. Fellow Celtics star Jaylen Brown also came up big in Sunday's win, scoring a game-high 26 points on 11-of-20 shooting in addition to six rebounds and three assists. Celtics big man Neemias Queta has taken a huge step forward in his development this season. That continued Sunday as he notched 18 points, seven rebounds, four assists, and three blocks against the Raptors. Jaylen Brown believes Queta should be up for the NBA's Most Improved Player award: "Neemi has been great. He's been just consistently getting better," he said. "In my opinion, he's probably one of the most improved players this year. I don't know if he's up for the award, but he should be.” Queta admitted that the Most Improved Player award crosses his mind often: “Yeah. I think about it all the time," Queta said. "I feel like I’ve made a good case for it… At the end of the day, I'm just helping the team win. That's my main goal. Obviously, that's secondary, the Most Improved (award).” Noa Dalzell joined NBC Sports Boston's all-female broadcast on Sunday and had a strong take on Celtics big man Neemias Queta: "I think he's a top 10 center in the NBA right now," Dalzell said. "He is the No. 1 reason, in my opinion, they are where they are as a team right now." NBC Sports Boston's all-female broadcast crew reacts after the Jays and Neemias Queta lead Boston to a 115-101 win over Toronto at TD Garden: Our All Female Postgame Live crew breaks down the Celtics' 115-101 win over the Raptors Celtics big man Neemias Queta recorded 15-plus points for the fourth consecutive game, finishing with 18 points (9-10 FG) along with seven rebounds, four assists, and three blocks. After the C's win, he caught up with Ashley Battle to talk about his big day: Score: 103-91 Celtics, 4:12 left in fourth quarter The Celtics have pulled away in the fourth, outscoring the Raptors 23-14 to take a 12-point lead with about four minutes left. Jayson Tatum leads the C's with 21 points. He earned his ninth double-double in 14 games, adding 13 rebounds and seven assists. Jaylen Brown has 10 points and five rebounds. Neemias Queta has stayed hot with 18 points, seven rebounds, and three blocks. Payton Pritchard has 15 points off the bench. Score: 80-77 Celtics The stage is set for a fun finish at TD Garden as the C's will take a three-point lead over the Raptors into the fourth quarter. Jaylen Brown has kept the C's ahead with a game-high 20 points (8-16 FG) along with five rebounds and three assists. Jayson Tatum has his ninth double-double in 14 games, as he's up to 17 points and 11 rebounds. Neemias Queta has 16 points, five boards, and three blocks. The Celtics lead despite turnovers (14) and an off day from 3-point range (6-24). They've looked solid defensively, however, limiting the Raptors to 43 percent shooting from the floor. Score: 78-75 Celtics, 2:00 left in third quarter The Celtics lead by three, but they'd be more comfortable late in this game against the Raptors if they had taken better care of the basketball. Toronto has 20 points off Boston's 14 turnovers. Score: 64-59 Celtics, 7:16 left in third quarter Jayson Tatum has his ninth double-double in his 14 games since returning from injury. The Celtics superstar is up to a game-high 17 points (5-10 FG) with 11 rebounds, three assists, and two steals. Neemias Queta has 16 points and five rebounds. Jaylen Brown has 14 points and five boards. Score: 54-46 Celtics The Celtics finished the second quarter on a 7-0 run to take a seven-point lead into the half at TD Garden. They outscored the Raptors 28-20 to overcome a slow start to the frame. Neemias Queta was the star for Boston in the first half, leading the team with 16 points (8-9 FG) while tallying five rebounds and an assist. Jaylen Brown scored 12 points (6-10 FG), five rebounds, and three assists. Jayson Tatum is up to 11 points (3-6 FG), eight rebounds, and three assists. Ja'Kobe Walter leads the Raptors with 12 points. Score: 38-36 Raptors, 6:07 left in second quarter Neemias Queta has helped the Celtics keep it close in the second quarter. Boston's big man leads the team with 12 points (6-7 FG) and has four rebounds in 10 minutes. Otherwise, the C's haven't looked all that sharp offensively since their strong start. They're shooting 42 percent from the floor, including just 3-of-16 from 3-point range. Score: 34-30 Raptors, 10:03 left in second quarter The Celtics called a quick timeout at the start of the second quarter after Toronto took the lead. The Raptors are on a 6-0 run and have outscored the C's 8-4 so far in the frame. Score: 26-26 We're tied up at TD Garden after a competitive first quarter between the Celtics and Raptors. Boston started on a 10-2 run, but Toronto answered with a 10-2 run of its own and slowed down the C's red-hot offense for the rest of the frame. The Celtics had four turnovers in the first 12 minutes. Neemias Queta led the Celtics with eight points, while Jayson Tatum and Baylor Scheierman chipped in five apiece. Tatum also tallied five rebounds. Score: 22-21 Celtics, 2:47 left in first quarter The Celtics started the game on a 10-2 run, but the Raptors answered with one of their own to tie the score at 12. They've kept it close, as Boston is holding on to a one-point lead with three minutes left in the opening quarter. For the second straight game, C's big man Neemias Queta has looked sharp in the first. He has a team-high eight points in eight minutes. Jayson Tatum has five points with five rebounds. Jaylen Brown has four points, and Baylor Scheierman added a 3-pointer off the bench. Ja'Kobe Walter leads Toronto with six points. Toronto is on a 6-0 run. Score: 10-2 Celtics, 9:07 left in first quarter The Celtics have been red-hot offensively, and that has continued so far today as they've gotten off to a strong start against Toronto at TD Garden. Neemias Queta has carried the momentum from his big night against Milwaukee into Sunday's action. The C's big man has six points (3-3 FG) in three minutes. Derrick White and Jaylen Brown have added two points apiece. White has a pair of assists and a steal. The Celtics have started 5-for-7 from the floor. The Raptors are 1-for-6. The Celtics on Sunday signed two-way player Ron Harper Jr. to a two-year NBA contract. C's coach Joe Mazzulla said of Harper before Sunday's game, "It's a testament to who he is. I'm really happy for him." Joe Mazzulla talks with Noa Dalzell about Ron Harper Jr. signing his first NBA contract with the Celtics Noa Dalzell joined NBC Sports Boston's broadcast on Sunday and spoke about Nikola Vucevic returning just in time for the Celtics' playoff run: "He's been dying to play in the playoffs, and he finally gets that chance." Celtics: Derrick White, Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum, Sam Hauser, Neemias Queta Raptors: Ja’Kobe Walter, RJ Barrett, Brandon Ingram, Scottie Barnes, Jacob Poeltl Nikola Vucevic arrives for his first game since March 6. The Celtics big man has missed the last month due to a fractured finger: Raptors coach Darko Rajaković spoke pregame about Jayson Tatum's performance since his return, and the Celtics' momentum heading into the playoffs: “Happy that (Tatum) is back and playing. They’re getting in a great rhythm now before the playoffs. This team is playing outstanding, on both ends of the floor. They’re a different team now than the start of the season.” Celtics big man Nikola Vucevic is officially cleared to return for Sunday's game against the Raptors. Boston's trade deadline addition hasn't played since March 6 due to a fractured finger. The C's have a clean injury report for Sunday's matchup. Chucky Hepburn (knee) and Immanuel Quickley (foot) are out for Toronto. Sunday's Celtics-Raptors game on NBC Sports Boston will feature an all-female broadcast with Abby Chin, Kayla Burton, Ashley Battle, Noa Dalzell, Aaliyah Edwards, and Aneesah Morrow. Coverage begins at 3 p.m. ET with Celtics Pregame Live.
